newsitem.title: USA: Sinclair TV stations to switch networks.
newsitem.headline: Sinclair TV stations to switch networks.

text.p: Sinclair Broadcast Group Inc on Monday said it was switching the affiliation of two television stations it owns and three it operates to the WB Television Network from the UPN Network.
Under the 10-year affiliation deal, WB guaranteed Sinclair total compensation of $64 million for the first eight years, and an additional $20 million in the final two years.

The deal, which takes effect on January 16, 1998, involves Sinclair-owned KRRT-TV in San Antonio and KOCB-TV in Oklahoma City. The three stations operated by Sinclair are WPTT-TV in Pittsburgh; WNUV-TV in Baltimore; WSTR-TV in Cincinnati.
WB is a unit of Time Warner Inc, and UPN is a unit of Chris-Craft Industries Inc, allied with Viacom Inc.
Sinclair owns or provides programming services to 29 television stations in 21 separate markets.
